en: The Extensive Record of Chan Master Hongzhi,
Volume One: Discourse Records from the Hall at Puzhao Chan Monastery in Sizhou,
Compiled by Attendant Jicheng.
When the Master was invited to Changlu, he held up the commentary and showed it to the assembly, saying:
"The path of language is cut off; the nature of words is empty."
Arriving here, one may truly say:
the whale has swallowed the seawater until it is exhausted,
revealing the coral branches.
Do you all understand?
If not yet, I trouble those who possess true knowledge once more.
He requested me to explain it for him.
Having finished composing the commentary,
the Master [received it] from the hands of the Changlu Worthy.
Having received the Dharma robe,
he held it up to present it,
saying: "The dhūta practitioners of Western India have waited for me for many years."
The practitioner of Dongshan transmitted the teaching at midnight;
they had just reached the summit of Dayu Ridge when,
despite exerting all their strength, they could not lift it.
Now, from the hall of Changlu, I hand this over with both hands.
Do you all understand the message within?
A single breath connects the branches in a shared moment of prosperity.
"Radiant wind brings spring to the tree-tops where no shadow lingers.

Have you all fully understood this? Having stepped across with your feet, you have already transcended the realm of both the mundane and the sacred;
your entire being is unimpeded within the functions of existence and non-existence.

Regarding the World-Honored One’s ascent of the seat one day: [Verse] The World-Honored One ascends the seat; The four assemblies look up with reverence. A single phrase is like a thunderclap; The entire world is deafened. If you can understand it here, You will see the Buddha’s original face. If you cannot understand it here, You will never meet the Buddha. [Commentary] The World-Honored One ascends the seat; the four assemblies look up with reverence. A single phrase is like a thunderclap; the entire world is deafened. If you can understand it here, you will see the Buddha’s original face. If you cannot understand it here, you will never meet the Buddha. This is the meaning of the verse. It is not that there is something else to be sought beyond this. If you can see it clearly right now, you will know that it has been so from the very beginning. If you do not yet understand, you must examine it further. Do not merely pass the time; you must investigate it thoroughly. If you can penetrate this, you will realize that the Buddhas and patriarchs have all transmitted this very thing. It is not that they have added anything new. If you can see it thus, you will be free from doubt. If you cannot see it thus, you must not be complacent. You must exert yourself to the utmost. If you can attain this understanding, you will be able to repay the profound kindness of the Buddhas and patriarchs. If you do not attain this understanding, you will remain lost in the cycle of birth and death. Therefore, you must strive with all your might. Do not let this opportunity pass. If you can understand it in this way, you will see that the ancient masters were not deceiving people. If you cannot understand it in this way, you are merely following words and chasing after shadows. You must realize that the Way is not something external; it is within your own mind. If you can see it thus, you will be at peace. If you cannot see it thus, you must not give up. You must continue to investigate until you reach a point where there is no more doubt. the Chapter on the Bodhisattva Purifying All Karmic Obstructions. Regarding the origins of realization, the handle is long.

A Verse for Tuo-an: The jade dragon sheds its remaining scales;

To understand elder brother Xuefeng’s paying homage to his original teacher: when Elder Brother Jie went south to see Master Xuefeng at Gujian, the cold spring water made him stare with wide-open eyes.
When one is thoroughly traceless, they have realized their own nature;
when turning back there is a path, who then can be named?
When the son returns to his father’s place, what need is there for seeking favor?
Clouds move toward the mountains without waiting for a breeze;
in the western neighbor’s house, the shuttle creaks as she weaves brocade—
within the shadow of the loom’s hub, fine threads fly silently.
Together with Master Bian’an, he caught the fragrant fish on the hook at Jia Shan;
he did not harbor anger over the staff and shouts of those days,
but went straight to the parting of the ways before the kalpa.
Only one who can externally transform by turning the pivot of the mechanism is a man of sinews beneath the eyebrows;
only such a person will accord with the tongueless man within the world.
Thoroughly illuminating one's own school, one knows its subtle and profound depths;
let the world come as it may, all rejoice with delight.
At Haishan, in the spring of the Gaiyin year.
Visiting Magistrate Wang Yuanming at Haishan in the Spring of Jia-yin after Rain.

The vine-covered gate is deep and secluded, with greenery leaning in graceful lines;
the fragrant flowers of pine and chrysanthemum mark the path of Yuanming,
while the profound beauty of stream and mountain belongs to the home of Mojue.
The Buddha-lamp of silent illumination remains cold and unshaken;

Yet I have heard that you are even more indolent than Layman Jue Rong.
The court birds have scattered the flowers in disarray several times.

with the wind it crosses forested ridges,
calling the moon to the window of the vines.
The resonance echoes through the empty valleys;
the sound soars unimpeded over the river.
Returning from my dream, the will of Heaven dawns.
The butterflies lose their pairs.

Now the clouds and waters settle in the meditation mats;

The body-cloud and mind-moon are fundamentally suchness (tathatā). Written by Wei Jinke,
Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices,

Roots and objects are transcended in vast clarity, wondrously without a trace.
Showing the Zen Practitioner Walking Amidst the Snow: Every household plants jade, filling the narrow lanes;

The single color of the ten directions—still bound by narrow constraints.

Fu Shiwu Lang Requests a Verse: Fu Shiwu Lang requests a verse: Dust and toil are dispelled as the hall becomes bright;
The numinous illumination of the empty mind merges before anything has sprouted.
Exhausting the source and reaching its limit, one realizes what has been attained from the beginning;
from the outset, one is equal to Buddhas and sentient beings.
Within this sphere of perfect emptiness, one attains true wandering.
Detached from water, the rhinoceros horn pierces through with a single point of autumnal clarity;
responding to circumstances without partiality, one ascends the Bird Path.
Wondrously identical to the bright moon, one remains still as the current flows.
On the eighth day of the month, I visited the lecturer Zhenwu of Xixi. Rain-like blossoms filled the seats, naturally fragrant and pure.
The tea bowls have just been set aside, their incense smoke curling in blue spirals;

Sengzhi’s spirit swallowed the Buddhas of the three periods of time.

A monk from Yunshan holds his almsbowl and begs for a verse; a monk from Yunshan holds his almsbowl and begs for a verse: "A thousand monks of the clouds and water plow in silence together."
I beg you to go forth from the mountains to seek alms:
Bracken and ferns sprout in the cold foothills under the night rain;

A single call in an empty valley is answered by an echo;
a perfect pearl unites with all colors to radiate light.
From here, one proceeds upward to distribute fragrant food.
I must first see Vimalakīrti.
Master Fang holds his almsbowl to beg for verses; Master Fang holds his almsbowl to beg for robes. At the break of dawn, he descended upon the city of Liancheng.
Wishing to divide the cooking and go to the upper realm,
one returns with a monk’s bowl of rice, satiated by three bamboo baskets;
there are honeycombs from bee-hives and the fragrance of a hundred flowers.
Willow threads and oriole companions harmonize with smooth, parted lips;
clouds and brocade illuminate the eyes of the people.
Observe their skillful maneuvers as they respond with fluidity and mastery.
Carrying dry wood wherever he goes, he is well-versed in the ways of the world.
To Layman Li, Layman Li: having washed away all residual confusion from within the chest of his withered meditation, a single point of empty luminosity remains, profound and still.
In every land and within every mote of dust, pure lands are formed;
from every flower and every leaf, the numinous root sprouts.
Without artifice, it resembles the moisture brought by clouds.

whether unrolling or rolling up, moving freely or remaining still, all is within me.
This person has truly attained the gateway of total mastery.
Seng Chanren Holds His Almsbowl and Seeks a Verse The myriad phenomena of the universe share the same root;

This is the wondrously luminous ground of the ancestral lineage.
Having thoroughly studied the monastic traditions, he entrusted them to his disciples;

The autumn sky stretches to the water, and the moon hangs in the twilight.
Five days after the start of spring, following the rhyme of Master Ben: Snow encircles the balustrades like the *Chu-cuo* chant;
Plum trees bear their first green fruit, and willow branches are supple.
The fragrance of mountain forests enters my new discourse;
wind and moon fill my breast as I follow the ancient precepts.
My dream rests upon my bent arm, for the spring lethargy is profound.
I beg you, like one with calloused hands from old age, what can you do?
The Rain Master and the Thunder Lord harbor much jealousy;

A Verse Requested by Chan Practitioner Liang for Tilling the Field A single field of fine soil stretches boundlessly;

Reaching the four boundaries of the field, who is there to be a companion?
The central tree itself blooms its flowers.
Showing it to people, the sickle’s shape appears as the autumn clouds roll away.

The flavor of the patch-robed monk is but slightly different from this.

lowering the plow amidst deep clouds to break the spring mist.
The subtle function of diligent cultivation is the business of our house.

What air of scholarly refinement does the attendant display in this portrait? What air of scholarly refinement does the attendant display in this portrait? His lofty character is nurtured like a pine that harbors medicinal fungi;
his winter-hardy form stands defiant against the snow and frost.

a lofty spirit is concentrated in the form of hills and valleys.
Like the moon after rain and clouds after a storm, the mind within his breast is serene and pure.
Autumn mountains and autumn waters, the corners of the eyes are azure.

This is the matter of the ten realms of existence reflecting their shadows within the Buddha-body.
Self and other interpenetrate; look into the mirror.

Wind and dust are wiped clean from face and eyes;

Through the proclamation of wondrous touch, the Buddha-son dwells in clarity.
In the Śūraṅgama Assembly there is such a person.
At that time, the Judicial Commissioner requested a verse: "The mirror of the mind is polished clean, with all wandering dust severed;
the numinous clarity of the original limit shines by itself as a divine spirit."

Master Xingyue requests a verse. Master Xingyue requests a verse. The night is clear and long, the moon travels through the sky.

Green oil, white tea, and black firewood;

Profoundly hidden at the tip of the Northern Dipper, one is permitted to drink dry the Western River; only then does one begin to compare [to the truth].
The three realms are suddenly liberated, with all images vanished.
The Layman Vimalakīrti’s livelihood is excellent;

The merit returns to the cold eyes beneath the double brows;
it illuminates the entire horizontal body at the beginning of kalpas beyond reckoning.
Dayang silently understood the intent of Dongsi.
Xuan Sha Ming’s letter to Xuefeng:

Able to accord with causes and conditions, not turning one's back on the truth;

The fragrance of alms-food fills the city, glowing like incense.

A Needle for Seated Meditation: This is the essential pivot of every Buddha and the vital point of every Patriarch;
it is knowing without being touched by phenomena.
It does not illuminate by confronting conditions;
it knows without contacting phenomena.
Its knowing is inherently subtle, illuminating without confronting conditions.
Its illumination is inherently wondrous;
its cognition is inherently subtle.
It is entirely devoid of discursive thought.
Its illumination is inherently wondrous;
it has never possessed even a hair’s breadth of a sign,
nor ever a thought of discrimination.
Its knowing is solitary and extraordinary,
never showing even the slightest sign of agitation;
its illumination is without grasping and yet fully clear.
The water is clear to the bottom;
the fish move slowly.
The sky is vast and boundless.
Birds fly into the distance.

Ruiyan Mountain in Siming is a preeminent location among mountain forests.
The chest is vast and open, swallowing and spitting forth wind and clouds;
the feet are relaxed and free, washing and polishing the tides and snow.
This is the Kaisei Aranya.
It stands at the very center.
Its azure eaves and patterned beams, its latticed windows and ornate screens,
shine brilliantly upon one another.
Carying staffs and wearing patched robes,

To awaken those in sleep and wakefulness,

To the west of the vast ocean lies an ancient monastery.
Travelers follow the path of birds to reach it and ascend its cloud-ladder.
Taking the groves as their model, companions in the saffron robes find refuge therein.
The compass and square are set forth, the knife and ruler are aligned.
Twelve peaks encircle it in a shimmering mass of green;
the great hall gathers the multitude, while the tiered pavilions rise into the void.
Who could have so purely bestowed upon me this Gong of Gaoping?
A vessel for the eternal Dharma-cave, it was offered from Dengshan with refined copper.
Hollow within and firm without, it proclaims the light and dispels the darkness.
Welcoming the moon to the gate, seeing off the crow as it descends Mount Dai;
the pestle strikes at the appointed time, its sound resonating without obstruction.
In a single thought, all is heard; within the myriad sensory realms, there is sovereign mastery.
The assembly from the ten directions resonates as one;
like bees drawn to fragrance, ants to scent, tigers to the wind, and dragons to the clouds,
honored guests and commoners find their order, and those who dwell together share in the sustenance.
Stately are the Dharma heirs; vast is the Buddha’s lineage.
The moon sinks as night draws to a close; the frost is clear and the dawn is cold.
The golden pitcher’s resonance has ceased; the jade water-clock’s flow is spent.
Deeply reflecting upon the dream-cushion is the Zen school’s correct contemplation (*samyag-darśana*).
When in motion, one follows its traces; when still, one attains its source.
One yearns for the subtle and wondrous sound, yet there is no direction in which it can be sought.
Relying on these grand melodies to guide those who dwell in the depths of obscurity;
their resonant sounds strike the ears, their crystalline clarity washes the mind.
The spirit responds as if in a valley, and the wind carries them across the forest.
Gradually and subtly, one returns to hearing the primordial source.
Roots and objects vanish as pairs, and the nature of awareness contains the void.
It is insufficient when grasped, yet more than enough when let go.
The true, perfectly clear, pure wisdom is suchness (*tathatā*).
Upon touching it, there is a sound like a thunderclap or the roar of a whale;
it is extinguished in that very place and born in that very place.
The shadow of the transformed butterfly disperses; the karmic debt of the fish is cleared.
Mountains and seas remain profound, yet heaven and earth achieve equilibrium.
Inscription for Benji Hermitage. The ultimate limit of reality (benji) is neither past, future, nor present.
How could it fall into any numerical categories? It is the wondrously perfect single mind.
This wondrously perfect single mind illuminates itself with spiritual clarity, transcending birth and death, and fusing the polarities of the absolute and the relative.
When the correct and the biased are blended and fused, one may forget their own effort within the Middle Way.
Like a phoenix soaring in a jade mirror, or a crane emerging from a silver cage—
abiding thus, Buddhas and Patriarchs attain it together.
